items.title: Source coverage and justified derivation
items.pass_criterion: Applicable upstream obligations (higher-level requirements, architecture allocations, hardware-software interface (HSI) obligations, approved constraints, or approved stakeholder/context inputs) are addressed; uncovered sources and derived requirements are identified and dispositioned. Coverage is semantic, not link-count based.
items.typical_defect: An allocated upstream need has no requirement, or a derived requirement has no rationale.

items.title: Behavioural completeness
items.pass_criterion: For applicable functions and modes the set captures start-up/initialisation, configured operation, boundary cases, invalid requests, fault detection and response, recovery/reset, shutdown and relevant state transitions. N/A scenarios are justified; no boilerplate for irrelevant modes.
items.typical_defect: Normal operation specified but invalid-request or recovery behaviour missing.

items.title: Non-functional and interface completeness
items.pass_criterion: Justified timing, resource, concurrency, data-integrity, safety, diagnostic, robustness and external-interface obligations are included where allocated. Budgets are not invented just to fill a category.
items.typical_defect: Allocated timing or interface constraint absent, or an unsourced budget added to fill a category.

items.title: Coherent structure and priorities
items.pass_criterion: The set is organised by function, interface, mode or variant, with stable identifiers and applicable priorities or release scopes, so it can be understood and maintained.
items.typical_defect: Flat unordered list with no grouping, variant or priority information.

items.title: Internal consistency and controlled redundancy
items.pass_criterion: No incompatible obligations or contradictory terms; duplicate and overlapping statements are removed or explicitly justified.
items.typical_defect: Two requirements prescribe different responses to the same condition.

items.title: Bidirectional traceability with consistency
items.pass_criterion: Relevant links to higher-level requirements and architecture (or approved stakeholder/context inputs where there is no higher level) exist in both directions, with evidence that linked meanings agree. No gratuitous duplicate trace paths.
items.typical_defect: Link exists but the linked requirement states a different condition or value.

items.title: Interdependency and feasibility analysis
items.pass_criterion: Dependencies, assumptions, parameter relationships and constraints are identified; feasibility is assessed and unresolved conflicts and decisions are recorded.
items.typical_defect: Coupled parameters specified independently with no recorded relationship or conflict.

items.title: Operating-environment impact analysed
items.pass_criterion: Effects on hardware, other software or systems, interfaces, start-up/reset behaviour, timing/resource use and interactions with the surrounding environment are evaluated as applicable.
items.typical_defect: No assessment of impact on shared resources or neighbouring elements.

items.title: Agreement, configuration and communication
items.pass_criterion: The approved baseline, revisions, open issues, affected parties and communication/approval status are identifiable. A generated draft is not an approved baseline by itself.
items.typical_defect: A generated file treated as the agreed baseline with no version or approval record.

items.title: Verification readiness
items.pass_criterion: Required outcomes can be linked to prospective verification measures; verification intent and unresolved verification ambiguities are recorded. Actual verification results belong to the downstream verification stages.
items.typical_defect: Requirements with no identifiable verification approach, or results claimed before verification.
